title: When the Room Turns
premise: Wren Montrose, a meticulous property surveyor, is hired to appraise Hollowmere House, a decaying estate whose previous owners all vanished mid-survey. As Wren documents the house, the mirrors begin reflecting rooms one second late, revealing that the house is not haunted but hungry — it was invited in generations ago by a Montrose ancestor who traded his family's belonging for power. Trapped inside as night falls, Wren must survive until sunrise while uncovering the inheritance clause binding their bloodline to the property. In the end, Wren refuses both escape and ownership, burning the deed and letting the house take them instead of the next heir — an act of sacrifice that finally starves it.
about_author: Hazel Quintana is a former building inspector from coastal Maine who spent a decade cataloguing condemned houses before turning to fiction. Her horror draws on real estate records, family ledgers, and the quiet dread of places that remember more than people do.

chapters.title: The Commission
chapters.summary: Wren accepts the Hollowmere appraisal job despite its strange history of vanished surveyors, motivated by debts and a need to belong somewhere professional. POV: Wren. Beat: uneasy ambition.

chapters.title: Inventory of Rooms
chapters.summary: First walkthrough; Wren photographs every room, noting the mirrors are covered with sheets no one remembers hanging. The house feels attentive. POV: Wren. Beat: creeping wrongness beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Deed in the Wall
chapters.summary: Behind plaster, Wren finds an 1897 deed signed by Ezekiel Montrose — their own surname — with a clause about 'perpetual invitation.' POV: Wren. Beat: personal stakes ignite.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: A hallway mirror reflects Wren's movement a beat behind. They test it scientifically, documenting timestamps, and the reflection begins testing them back. POV: Wren. Beat: rationality cracking.

chapters.title: The Neighbor's Warning
chapters.summary: Elderly neighbor Odile Vasseur tells Wren the house 'appraises back' and begs them to leave before dark, mentioning her sister was the last surveyor. POV: Wren. Beat: dread confirmed by witness.

chapters.title: Locked In
chapters.summary: At dusk every door and window seals itself; phone signal dies. Wren realizes the appraisal appointment was never theirs to end. POV: Wren. Beat: trap springs.

chapters.title: The Long Hour
chapters.summary: Wren maps the sealed house, discovering rooms have rearranged since morning. The documentation notebook becomes their anchor to reality. POV: Wren. Beat: fragile control.

chapters.title: Ezekiel's Ledger
chapters.summary: In the study, Wren reads the ancestor's ledger: payments made in 'belonging,' entries where family names are struck out one by one. POV: Wren. Beat: inheritance revealed as predation.

chapters.title: The Second Reflection
chapters.summary: Mirrors now show the room as it was decades ago — a family at dinner, all facing the glass, smiling too long. POV: Wren. Beat: the past is watching.

chapters.title: Odile at the Window
chapters.summary: Odile appears outside at 2 a.m., mouthing warnings; the house shows Wren a mirror-vision of Odile dead, then she's simply gone. POV: Wren. Beat: isolation deepens.

chapters.title: What Was Invited
chapters.summary: Wren deciphers the clause: each generation must 'renew the invitation' or the house takes what it's owed. The last renewal was 1974 — overdue. POV: Wren. Beat: rules established.

chapters.title: The Attic Census
chapters.summary: Attic holds portraits of every vanished surveyor, faces freshly painted over. One canvas is still wet, bearing Wren's outline. POV: Wren. Beat: fate made visible.

chapters.title: Rooms That Remember
chapters.summary: The nursery replays a child's voice counting down hours till dawn; Wren realizes the house measures time differently than they do. POV: Wren. Beat: clock anxiety.

chapters.title: The Bargain Offered
chapters.summary: Through a mirror, a figure in Ezekiel's likeness offers Wren ownership of Hollowmere — wealth, permanence, belonging — if they sign the renewal. POV: Wren. Beat: temptation.

chapters.title: Refusal and Consequence
chapters.summary: Wren refuses; the house retaliates, unmaking corridors, trapping them in the cellar where the walls breathe. POV: Wren. Beat: punishment for defiance.

chapters.title: Cellar of Names
chapters.summary: Cellar walls are inscribed with thousands of names, including Odile's sister. Wren adds nothing, but their name appears anyway, faint. POV: Wren. Beat: erasure threat.

chapters.title: The Surveyor Before
chapters.summary: Wren finds the 1974 surveyor's hidden notes: she survived by staying 'unremarkable' — never naming herself, never claiming anything. POV: Wren via found document. Beat: strategy emerges.

chapters.title: Becoming No One
chapters.summary: Wren strips identifying marks, speaks in third person, documents the house without documenting themselves. It works — briefly. POV: Wren. Beat: self-erasure as survival.

chapters.title: The House Speaks
chapters.summary: The house uses Wren's mother's voice through the pipes, offering comfort, then accusation: 'You were always looking for a room of your own.' POV: Wren. Beat: psychological siege.

chapters.title: Midnight Inventory
chapters.summary: Halfway point. Wren takes stock: four hours to dawn, one flashlight, one notebook, no exits. They choose to fight rather than hide. POV: Wren. Beat: resolve hardens.

chapters.title: The Mirror Corridor
chapters.summary: Wren walks the hall of mirrors deliberately, stepping into the one-second gap between reflection and reality — and glimpses the house's true interior: a throat. POV: Wren. Beat: revelation.

chapters.title: Ezekiel's Confession
chapters.summary: A preserved letter reveals Ezekiel didn't summon the house to gain power — he sold his family's belonging to escape poverty, and regretted it instantly. POV: Wren via letter. Beat: ancestor humanized.

chapters.title: The Heir Clause
chapters.summary: Wren learns any Montrose who enters inherits the debt; they weren't hired by chance. Someone alive sent them here deliberately. POV: Wren. Beat: betrayal foreshadowed.

chapters.title: The Client Calls
chapters.summary: A rotary phone rings; the client — lawyer Aldous Renner — admits he engineered the assignment on behalf of the surviving Montrose trust. He wants the house fed. POV: split Wren/Renner call. Beat: human villain surfaces.

chapters.title: Renner's Arrival
chapters.summary: Renner arrives at the threshold at 3 a.m., unable to enter, instructing Wren to sign. Wren records his confession on the survey camera. POV: Wren. Beat: evidence secured.

chapters.title: The House Turns
chapters.summary: Enraged by exposure, the house stops pretending: walls become wet wood, mirrors flood, and the portraits open their eyes. POV: Wren. Beat: full horror unleashed.

chapters.title: Chase Through the Floor Plan
chapters.summary: A relentless pursuit through shifting rooms; Wren survives by thinking like a surveyor, reading the house's geometry against it. POV: Wren. Beat: competence under terror.

chapters.title: The Child in the Glass
chapters.summary: Wren finds the counting child from the nursery trapped in a mirror — the first Montrose daughter, never renewed, never taken. She shows Wren the hearth where the original invitation burns. POV: Wren. Beat: ally found.

chapters.title: Terms of Belonging
chapters.summary: The daughter explains: the house runs on claimed belonging. Anything Wren claims, it owns. To destroy it, Wren must claim everything — then give it away. POV: Wren. Beat: plan formed.

chapters.title: Claiming Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Wren signs the renewal — but writes themselves as owner of the entire estate, every room, every mirror. The house exults, believing it has won. POV: Wren. Beat: gambit.

chapters.title: Owner of the Throat
chapters.summary: As owner, Wren can see the house whole: its hunger, its fear of vacancy. They begin formally deeding away each room — to the dead, to the town, to no one. POV: Wren. Beat: reversal executed.

chapters.title: Renner's Greed
chapters.summary: Renner breaks through the weakening threshold to seize the 'valuable' property and is absorbed by the first room he claims. His recorded confession remains. POV: Wren observing. Beat: villain consumed by his own scheme.

chapters.title: The Last Room
chapters.summary: Only the hearth room remains, holding the original invitation contract. The house offers Wren everything one final time — belonging, forever. POV: Wren. Beat: ultimate temptation.

chapters.title: Sunrise Clause
chapters.summary: Dawn light touches the windows; the house weakens, desperate. Wren burns the invitation and the deed together in the hearth, renouncing all claim, all inheritance, all belonging. POV: Wren. Beat: climax sacrifice.

chapters.title: What the Fire Takes
chapters.summary: The house collapses inward, taking Wren with it — but the mirrors release the trapped daughter and every struck-out name into the morning air. POV: omniscient. Beat: cost and mercy entwined.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Appraisal
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Renner's firm receives Wren's final survey: complete documentation of a house that no longer exists, ending with Wren's own name crossed out — by their own hand. POV: epistolary. Beat: grief and awe.

chapters.title: Odile's Testimony
chapters.summary: Odile Vasseur tells investigators what she saw at the window that night, and gives them her sister's name back. The vanished are declared dead; the land is left wild. POV: Odile. Beat: mourning and closure.

chapters.title: The Empty Lot
chapters.summary: The lot where Hollowmere stood grows nothing but mirror-smooth puddles after rain. Passersby feel watched, then — slowly — less so. POV: omniscient. Beat: lingering unease fading.

chapters.title: Belonging to No Room
chapters.summary: Final chapter: a new young surveyor finds one of Wren's field notebooks in a secondhand shop, reads it cover to cover, and chooses, wisely, to leave the last page unphotographed. POV: new character. Beat: inheritance refused, story ended.
